summary: Vault unlock: the browser fetches salt/KDF params (real or a deterministic decoy), derives Master Key and Auth Key, sends only the Auth Key, and on success gets a session plus the wrapped DEK — with a transparent stale-KDF re-wrap and an idle lock that discards the entire in-memory model.

read.role: the single password screen, in full-login and re-unlock modes
input and error-state conventions for the password screen, and the shell that carries the default KDF envelope and hosts the re-unlock screen

endpoints.login: POST /api/auth/login { username, authKey } -> { wrappedDek, dekNonce, kdfStale } and sets session cookie
endpoints.rewrap: POST /api/auth/rewrap { salt, kdf, authKey, wrappedDek, dekNonce } — authenticated, replaces all five stored fields in one transaction

decoySalt.value: HMAC(server_secret, normalized_username) truncated to 16 bytes, paired with the server's current default KDF envelope, for an unknown username

unknownUsernameLoginBehavior.value: runs a full Argon2id verification against a fixed decoy hash and discards the result, so timing does not reveal existence

serverSideAuthKeyHash.value: Argon2id, starting point 64 MiB memory, 2 iterations, constant-time comparison — defense in depth, not the primary work factor

sessionCookie.value: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; carries only an opaque session token, no key material, no user id

sessionLifetime.value: absolute 12 hours from issue, not sliding

idleLock.value: user-configurable 5-60 minutes, default 15, stored as idleLockMinutes in the encrypted profile record (absent = 15)

idleLockDiscard.value: discards Master Key, DEK, and every decrypted value derived from them (whole in-memory model, rendered figures, chart series, cached plaintext); the one named exception is unsaved form input in the open form

rewrapSaltSize.value: fresh 128-bit salt generated for the re-wrap

rewrapFailureBehavior.value: session continues on old parameters if the rewrap POST fails; retried on next login, never locks the user out

sessionRotation.value: session id is rotated (new session id) on every successful login

fixtures: a real user at current KDF parameters and a nonexistent username, for the salt-fetch and login timing/shape-indistinguishability assertions
a real user with a deliberately stale KDF envelope, for the transparent-upgrade assertion (salt/envelope/Auth-Key-hash/wrapped-DEK all change, DEK proven unchanged)
a record written before a KDF upgrade, to prove decryptability survives the re-wrap
a stubbed /api/auth/rewrap returning 500, for the 'stays logged in on rewrap failure' criterion
focus: timing-indistinguishability criteria (salt fetch, login) need actual statistical timing measurement across many trials, not a single-run assertion

the idle-lock criterion must assert against the in-memory model itself (no decrypted name/value/snapshot reachable), not just that the key handles are null — a test that only checks the key variables would pass a broken implementation that leaves data cached elsewhere
'no key material in localStorage/sessionStorage at any point' needs an assertion that runs throughout the flow, not just at the end, since a leak-then-clear bug would otherwise pass
the stale-envelope account is deliberately distinguishable from a decoy (Rules) — do not write or accept a test asserting otherwise; only the current-KDF-parameters case is asserted indistinguishable
